source.title: Asymptotics of Wide Networks from Feynman Diagrams

record.tranche_reason: Reports training outcomes for fully connected networks on two-class MNIST, an additional setting for the training-error claim.
record.gate_note: The reported correlation-function and NTK results do not measure training classification error. Figure 10 reports that all runs reached training accuracy 1; rows capture its separately plotted width, activation, and depth conditions.
record.test_reason: The study reports perfect training accuracy for fully connected linear and tanh networks on two-class MNIST. V1 specifies convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, so these results do not test that version. Its other results concern correlation-function asymptotics, NTK evolution and Hessian spectra, without testing V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that their correlation-function conjecture holds in all tested cases, prove it in restricted cases, tighten training-dynamics bounds and derive leading finite-width corrections supported by experiments. Perfect training accuracy is an experimental detail, not their central conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies fully connected networks on two-class MNIST with MSE training for network-evolution experiments, rather than the cited CIFAR classification recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The figure reports tanh and linear activations, one and two hidden layers, and widths n=128 and n=1024; the caption states all runs reached training accuracy 1.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 10 reports training accuracy 1 for all eight fully connected linear/tanh configurations, with one or two hidden layers and widths 128 or 1024, trained on 20 two-class MNIST examples at learning rate 0.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fully connected linear and tanh networks can attain zero training classification error on this small two-class MNIST task.

fits_no_version.finding: The study derives and empirically checks width-dependent correlation-function bounds, finite-width NTK corrections and relations between Hessian and NTK spectra.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wide-network dynamics admit an asymptotic expansion with leading finite-width corrections that approximate the tested networks' evolution.

record.problems: Training-accuracy result is reported in a figure caption without per-run numerical detail or uncertainty; the described task is two-class MNIST, not CIFAR.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported result directly measures training classification accuracy.

untested.parts: All: no convolutional-network training-error results on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted-label conditions or recipe comparisons.
All: no ReLU teacher-student comparison measuring spurious minima with matched versus extra student neurons.
All: no training-error comparison of deep plain convolutional networks with shallower or residual networks.
All: no initialization comparison measuring learning speed or trainable depth; Gaussian versus binary initialization experiments measure correlation-function scaling.
All: no loss-and-curvature trajectories establishing recovery above an initial stability limit, edge-of-stability training, or divergence relative to that threshold.
All: no batch-normalization comparison or Fixup training-speed and stability comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The Figure 10 accuracy statement is valid; cannot_determine describes its inability to establish the specified versions, not uncertainty about the reported accuracy. Single runs and the absence of per-condition accuracy curves do not themselves invalidate the caption's result.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, convolutional networks, corrupted or random labels, SGD or Adam comparison, smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
